transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you and what brings you in today?

I’ve been having a hard time keeping things organized at work. I work with customer jobs, tickets, receipts, and notes, and lately it all just ends up piled together. Then I can’t tell what I’m supposed to handle first, and it’s been getting really frustrating.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve been especially sad, and I don’t think I’ve lost interest in things. Mostly I’m just frustrated with how things have been going.
Have you been feeling unusually worried or anxious about things lately, even when there isn't a clear reason for it?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get stressed when things pile up, but I wouldn’t say I’m unusually anxious for no reason. It’s more tied to what’s going on in front of me.
Have you been having trouble concentrating or staying focused on tasks, even when they’re important?

Yes. I’ll start going over the day’s dry-cleaning orders, and at first I’m fine. But after a few minutes my mind drifts off to other things, like labels I need to check, choir plans, or something going on at home. Then I come back to it and realize I missed half of what I was supposed to be checking.
Do you find yourself acting impulsively or interrupting others often, especially during conversations or tasks?

Yes, I do. At work I’ll cut into my staff’s conversations, or I’ll reach over and fix how they’re sorting clothes before they even ask me. I know it probably comes off like I’m butting in, but in the moment I just do it.

Do you find that these difficulties with staying focused and acting impulsively happen in other areas of your life, like at home or in social situations, or are they mostly limited to when you’re at work?

It’s not just at work, no. Work is where it shows the most, because the shop has had late orders and I’ve mixed up billing, and then staff or customers get tense with me.

But it happens outside work too. At church, I used to help lead some planning, but I’ve stepped back from that because people were getting frustrated with me. So it’s kind of showing up in more than one part of my life.
When did you first start noticing these kinds of difficulties with focus or impulsivity? Were they something you experienced even as a child, like before your teenage years?

Yes, it goes back that far. Even in grade school, teachers would tell my mother I was bright, but scattered. I talked out of turn a lot, lost papers, and needed reminders to finish my work. So it wasn’t something that just started recently.
